device.model: OpenLH liquid handler on a uArm Swift Pro
device.name: OpenLH liquid handler (uArm Swift Pro)

facts.text: The OpenLH is a liquid handling system based on the uArm Swift Pro robotic arm
SwiftWithUltrasonic is the API wrapper of swift and swift_pro; its defaults are dev_port=None, baud=115200, filters={'hwid': 'USB VID:PID=2341:0042'} and ultrasonic_port='D8'
get_position calls P2220 and returns an [x, y, z] float array of the arm's current location
get_polar calls P2221 and returns an [rotation, stretch, height] float array
The servo numbers are SERVO_BOTTOM 0, SERVO_LEFT 1, SERVO_RIGHT 2 and SERVO_HAND 3
get_servo_angle returns an array of float, or one float when a servo id is given, and reads P2200/P2206
set_servo_angle sends G202 N<servo> V<angle> and documents 0 - 180 degrees
set_position sends G0 with X, Y, Z and F values; it documents x, y and z in mm and speed in mm/sec, and its return comment says the device returns ok even out of range
set_pump writes the pump service value on or off and returns True when the reply starts with 'ok'
set_gripper writes the gripper service value on or off and returns True when the reply starts with 'ok'
get_ultrasonic calls 'get value' on the ultrasonic node and returns an int distance in cm
get_limit_switch reads P2233 and returns True for 'ok V1' and False for 'ok V0'
get_is_moving reads M2200 and returns True for 'ok V1' and False for 'ok V0'
The SwiftAPI class defines no motion stop, abort or halt method; its only connection-level stop is close_conn, and reset attaches the servos and moves to the default position
The README says the arm runs a custom Marlin firmware and the OpenLH compiles Swift API calls to G-code over UART
